_README: Edge structure for the 20-node hybrid CPS network.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. The previous graph connected every pair of active
devices -- a complete graph. With three nodes that is unremarkable and
needed no defence. At many nodes a complete graph is a modelling CHOICE, and
an undefended one is indistinguishable from 'whatever scored best'.
EDGE SEMANTICS, stated before any result was looked at:
an edge joins two nodes that monitor the SAME PHYSICAL PROCESS
and is therefore expected to share genuine mechanical coupling. That is the
only relation a graph over sensors can carry that is not circular: joining
nodes because their scores correlate would be fitting the topology to the
thing the topology is supposed to explain.
Three process groups, plus a sparse backbone between group representatives
standing for the shared monitoring segment (all twenty report to one
gateway, so a network-wide event has SOME path, but not a direct one
between every pair). Density is 60/190 = 32% of a complete graph: 21 edges
within group A, 21 within B, 15 within C, and 3 on the inter-group backbone.
GROWN FROM THE ORIGINAL 10-NODE NETWORK (esp32-sim-11..20 added) to equalise
sensor-type representation -- 10 MPU6050-type + 10 SW-420-type -- once
esp32-vib-002 (SW-420) had a real captured session to calibrate the new
SW-420-type simulated nodes against (config/simulated_nodes.json's
sw420_measured). The original 10 nodes and their SCENARIOS anomaly
assignments (scripts/generate_network_data.py) are UNCHANGED -- the ten new
nodes are added as additional healthy context within their group, not as
new anomaly targets, so the original adversarial scenario design (SCENARIO_C
spread across non-adjacent nodes, etc.) stays exactly as documented and
comparable to prior results.
GROUP A is where the two REAL nodes sit, together, because they physically
do: esp32-vib-001 (MPU6050) and esp32-vib-002 (SW-420) are mounted on the
same bench surface, which is what makes the C4 simultaneous-disturbance
condition a coupled event rather than two coincidences.
WHAT THIS TOPOLOGY MUST NOT BE USED FOR. It was not selected by scoring
candidate topologies on validation and keeping the winner. It is the
physical layout, written down. If a future experiment DOES search over
topologies, that search must run on validation only and be reported as a
search.

A.label: Bench 1 -- both physical nodes plus five simulated peers
A.rationale: The two real boards share one bench surface; sim-03/04/11 (MPU6050-like) and sim-12/13 (SW-420-like) stand for further sensors on the same machine, grown to keep group A's sensor-type mix balanced after the network-wide equalisation.

B.label: Machine group 2
B.rationale: Independent machine; originally one switch-type node among two accelerometer-type, now four switch-type (07/15/16/17) among three accelerometer-type (05/06/14) -- the group carrying most of the added SW-420-type nodes.

C.label: Machine group 3
C.rationale: Independent machine carrying the two original hard cases (weak anomalies, slow-developing fault) plus sim-18 (a third frequency band) and sim-19/20 (switch-type analogues of the same two hard-case philosophies).

edge_rules.intra_group: complete within each group -- same physical process, genuine mechanical coupling
edge_rules.inter_group: one edge between designated representatives only -- shared monitoring segment, not shared physics
edge_rules.directionality: UNDIRECTED. Mechanical coupling is symmetric; adjacency is symmetrised and the normalisation D^-1/2 (A + wI) D^-1/2 assumes it.
edge_rules.self_loop: weight GNN_SELF_LOOP_WEIGHT, swept on VALIDATION only -- see results/gnn_baselines/self_loop_sweep.json

activity_gate: An edge is only realised between two nodes BOTH heard from within
GNN_EDGE_WINDOW_SECONDS. A silent node keeps its self-loop and nothing
else, so a device that drops off the network cannot keep influencing its
neighbours' scores with a stale reading.
